title: Redundant Connection
summary: A tree got one extra edge. Find the edge you can delete to turn the graph back into a tree.

tests.explain: The three edges form the triangle 1-2-3. Removing any of them leaves a tree, and [2, 3] is the one listed last.
1-2-3-4-1 is a cycle. Of its four edges, [1, 4] appears last in the input. [1, 5] is not on the cycle, so removing it would disconnect node 5.
The cycle 1-2-3 closes at the third edge. The answer does not have to be the last edge of the whole list.

hints: A tree has no cycles, so the extra edge created exactly one cycle. Any edge on that cycle could be removed; the problem wants the one that appears last in the input.
Add the edges one by one. Which edge is the first one whose two ends are already connected by the edges added before it?
With union-find, union(a, b) finds both roots. If they are equal, a and b were already connected and [a, b] is the answer. That edge is automatically the cycle's last edge in input order.

complexity.time: O(n · α(n)): one union per edge, each almost O(1)
